narrative:
On July 31, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,307 cases across 58 judge listings, successfully hearing 879 matters to achieve an overall hearing rate of 38.1%. This performance reflects a gradual decline compared to prior recorded sessions, including July 28 (39.5% of 2,610 scheduled cases), July 20 (44.5% of 2,620 scheduled cases), and July 17 (49.2% of 2,108 scheduled cases).

Individual judge throughput varied considerably across court halls. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty recorded the highest total volume of heard matters, completing 83 out of 192 scheduled cases (43.2%). Strong conversion rates were demonstrated by division benches, such as Mohammad Nawaz & G. Basavaraja, who heard 19 of 22 cases (86.4%), and D. K. Singh & T. M. Nadaf, who completed 21 of 28 listed matters (75.0%). Conversely, heavy dockets constrained progress in several halls; Justice Suraj Govindaraj heard 0 of 120 listed matters in Court Hall 10, while Justice B. M. Shyam Prasad addressed 19 of 147 scheduled cases (12.9%) in Court Hall 6.

Analysis by hearing stage shows that matters listed for Orders achieved the highest conversion among major categories, with 378 of 840 cases heard (45.0%), whereas Final Hearings registered the lowest clearance rate at 25.5% (85 of 333 cases). Admission matters logged a 35.4% conversion rate (163 of 460 cases). In terms of case types, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the roster with 960 scheduled items and a 34.7% hearing rate (333 heard), down from 39.9% on July 28. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) maintained higher clearance at 47.4% (164 of 346 cases), while Writ Appeals (WA) led overall case type conversion at 77.8% (28 of 36 cases heard).
